chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, saying: Al-Mi'za narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who prays behind an Imam and salutes (ends his prayer) before the Imam, he said: 'There is no harm in that.' And if a congregation prays in a mosque, it is not permissible for another group to pray immediately after with a new Adhan and Iqamah.

That was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abu Ali, who said: We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man came to him and said: 'I am your ransom, we prayed Fajr in the mosque, some of us left and some sat in the mosque for Tasbih. A man entered the mosque and gave the Adhan, so we prevented him and kept him from doing so. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You did well, keep him from it and prevent him strongly.'
I said: 'And if they enter and wish to pray there as a congregation?' He said: 'They stand in a corner of the mosque and their Imam does not precede them (in taking the main space).'

I said to him: 'I am your ransom, we have an Imam who is different (from your school), and he dislikes all our companions.' He said: 'What does it matter to you what he says? By Allah, if you are truthful, you are more entitled to the mosque than he is. So be the first to enter and the last to leave, and have good character with people and speak good.'
A man said: 'I am your ransom, the saying of Allah the Exalted:
And speak to people good words
Is it for all people?' He smiled and said: 'It is not specific (to all), say: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.'
And that which indicates what we said, that they do not give Adhan or Iqamah whenever they wish to pray as a congregation.

key_terms.إقامة: Iqamah (second call to prayer immediately before standing)
key_terms.مخالفاً: Different/contrasting (referring to a different school or group)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when multiple groups want to pray in the same mosque at different times?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of multiple congregations praying in a single mosque, distinguishing between a continuous flow of prayer and distinct sessions marked by new Adhan and Iqamah. It further establishes the principle of 'first-come, first-served' for mosque occupancy, affirming that even if a rival Imam's followers arrive later, the original congregation retains priority, provided they maintain excellent character (husn al-khuluq) as a practical manifestation of their faith.
